category_description: Federal income tax, payroll tax and other taxes in the United States.
subcategory_description: The taxes taken from pay and from self-employment income.
subject_name: Social Security and Medicare Payroll Tax (FICA)
label: Social Security tax rate, each for employee and employer
context: Employees and employers each pay this rate, 12.4% in total. It applies only up to the wage base.

label: Medicare tax rate, each for employee and employer
context: Employees and employers each pay this rate, 2.9% in total. There is no wage base limit.

label: Social Security wage base
context: The most in earnings that is subject to Social Security tax for the year. Medicare tax has no limit. Also called the contribution and benefit base or the taxable maximum.

label: Additional Medicare tax rate
context: Applies to Medicare wages, self-employment income, and railroad retirement compensation above the threshold for your filing status. There is no employer match.

label: Additional Medicare tax: employer withholding threshold
context: Employers withhold the additional tax on wages paid above this amount in a calendar year, whatever the employee's filing status.

label: Additional Medicare tax threshold, married filing jointly
context: The threshold on your tax return for married couples filing jointly.

label: Additional Medicare tax threshold, married filing separately
context: The threshold on your tax return for married people filing separately. All other filers use the same amount as the employer withholding threshold.

subject_intro: The Social Security and Medicare payroll tax rates, the Social Security wage base, and how the Additional Medicare Tax works for high earners.
